# Set 45 candidate publication and seed contract — draft

Status: review draft, NOT frozen. No runtime or expected vectors are authorized by this document alone. Root's engineering direction selects conditional A→A+1 and exact-target checkpoint plus 60 target descendants for the candidate profile. This is not Mike D78, a production authority, result finality, a consensus change or an unbiasedness guarantee. Set 44 remains byte-compatible. Featured rounds, pairing, bouts, awards, transfers and public-chain publication are outside this slice.

## 1. Concrete authority and scope

Add `gymseed` (durable journal/pure codecs) and `seednode` (normal-PoW owned-fixture node/publisher adapter). One parent-owned journal consumes the exact complete receipt from a concrete `*gymevent.Store`, with one original authenticated `gymstable.Session` and its matching concrete entry store. Exported JSON is never source authority.

The publication chain is permanently the established **zero256** child's primary/peer chain home. Derive its account/source IDs from the trusted Set 44 Pin and existing validated child marker; never use the currently selected child's chain by default. A seed operation can borrow the actual zero256 owned node pair only while that child is already running. Stop/logout cancel and join the borrow before node closure. Switching to incrementing256, node unavailability or restart never changes the pinned home. There is no automatic Start, bootstrap mining, third chain, wallet RPC widening or public endpoint option.

The publisher is a separate purpose-fixed capability attached by the actual node owner, not a gym View, arbitrary RPC config or caller-supplied verification flag. The new `gymaccount.SeedPublish` capability permits only a fresh, enrolled, non-recovery-required **unheld login session**. Mining tokens refuse it. Parent capability checks retain the exact original session/view and signed-in/nonbusy publication guard. Core Publish/Attest additionally require zero256. View permits Prepare, retained reads and read-only Reconcile (including held sessions); node-offline is explicit when no correct live publisher borrow exists.

Funding belongs to a separate published operator fixture, not either gym wallet: secp256k1 scalar 1, compressed public key, native P2WPKH on the unchanged normal Phase-A network. Maximum coin value is the unchanged consensus MaxSatoshi; positive int64 only. No funding transfer is implemented. Existing mining payout remains unchanged. Absent funds means `seed_waiting_for_funds`; a scan that has not established inventory means `seed_scan_incomplete`. Tests explicitly fund the fixture on their isolated chain; runtime never mines or spends another wallet to manufacture funds.

Use two distinct published Ed25519 fixtures. Their 32-byte seeds are SHA256 of the exact ASCII/NUL strings `SLUG candidate seed declaration fixture\0v1\0` and `SLUG candidate seed checkpoint fixture\0v1\0`; public keys follow standard Ed25519 derivation. These public test materials are not credentials or operator keys. Only purpose-specific declaration and exact retained-target checkpoint signing exists. No generic sign-message/key-file API is introduced. Normal builds reject `slugtestpow`; scoped `slugtestclock` composition is separate and never a release build.

## 2. Definitions, ordering and identity

All `\0` notation here means one actual NUL byte. `H` is SHA256; `J(T)` is canonical UTF-8 JSON using the exact field order below, compact separators, no HTML escaping, no trailing LF. All strings are ASCII and enumerated or fixed-length lowercase hex. `LP(b)=LE32(len(b))||b`; `ID(x)` in binary preimages means decode the 64-character display-order hex directly into 32 bytes. This differs from wire internal block-hash byte order; block/header parsing must explicitly convert via its normal display hash. Public integers are unsigned canonical base10 except positive millisecond timestamps represented by signed int64 and the explicitly enumerated signed scan heights (-1 initial sentinel); no exponents, fractions, signs, negative zero or values beyond stated bounds.

`PublisherChainID = H("SLUG candidate publication chain\0v1\0" || ID(SourceStoreID) || ID(zero256.AccountID) || ID(zero256.Source.AuthorityID) || ID(Genesis))`.

`EventKey = H("SLUG candidate seed event\0v1\0" || LE32(Network) || ID(Genesis) || ID(SourceStoreID) || ID(event.EventID) || PublisherPublicKeyRaw32)`.

Here event.EventID is the complete Set44 gymevent.Event.EventID, not its nested entry SourceEventID; SourceStoreID is gymevent.ID(source Pin). This conflict key excludes seed StoreID, rule/target choices, snapshot/receipt digest, transaction, actor, generation, signature and observation time. They cannot create another identity for the same authority/source event.

`StoreID = H("SLUG candidate seed store\0v1\0" || LP(J(Pin)))`.

Rules are the exact ordered object `{"version":1,"target":"first_anchor_next_block","floor":"genesis_inclusive","carrier":"SLUGSEED-v1","finality":"exact_target_checkpoint_60","max_step_blocks":8,"max_scan_restarts":16,"fee_satoshis":1000}`. `RulesID=H("SLUG candidate seed rules\0v1\0"||LP(J(Rules)))`.

The scan floor is always height0 and the normal genesis hash, inclusively. It is never supplied by a browser or selected from a later tip. The journal's initialized creation time must be strictly before the selected event cutoff. Its immutable Pin/rules/floor are synced before sampling that creation time. A late new journal cannot retroactively activate an old event. No per-Saturday preregistration is required. A complete late-captured Set 44 receipt remains acceptable for a journal activated before C. Official rule changes remain subject to existing D63; this profile activates no official rule.

## 3. Exact core DTOs and canonical order

Field lists below are normative JSON order and spelling; their scalar types are Go types. Slices are non-null, arrays exact length, optional pointers null only where stated. All 64-hex IDs and 32-byte public keys are lowercase; compressed secp keys are66 hex, Ed25519 signatures128 hex. Normal chain network/genesis and published fixture selectors are fixed, not runtime overrides.

- `Pin`: `version uint32=1; source_store_id string; source_pin gymevent.Pin; publisher_gym_id string; publisher_account_id string; publisher_source_authority_id string; publisher_chain_id string; network uint32; genesis string; floor_height uint32=0; floor_hash string=genesis; publisher_public_key string; checkpoint_public_key string; funding_public_key string; funding_script string; rules_id string`.
- `Info`: `version uint32=1; store_id string; pin Pin; created_at_ms int64; event_count uint32; funding_height int32; funding_hash string; funding_complete bool; funding_generation uint32; funding_restart_count uint32`. Funding generation0..16 equals funding_restart_count. Funding height is a signed scan-height field: -1 means no genesis scan yet, with empty hash and false complete; otherwise0..MaxInt32 and hash required.
- `Declaration`: `version uint32=1; event_key string; store_id string; source_store_id string; event gymevent.Event; snapshot_digest string; receipt_digest string; publisher_chain_id string; network uint32; genesis string; floor_height uint32=0; floor_hash string; rules_id string; publisher_public_key string; checkpoint_public_key string`. No actor/time/nonce or caller target.
- `SignedDeclaration`: `version uint32=1; declaration Declaration; signature string`.
- `Outpoint`: `txid string; index uint32`.
- `FundingCoin`: `outpoint Outpoint; value_satoshis int64; script string; block_height uint32; block_hash string; coinbase bool`.
- `Publication`: `version uint32=1; raw_tx string; txid string; coin FundingCoin; built_at_ms int64; dispatch_count uint32; first_dispatch_at_ms int64; last_dispatch_at_ms int64; state string`. `raw_tx` is exact lower-hex full wire transaction. State=`retained|unknown|submitted`; count0 iff retained, both dispatch times0 iff count0; otherwise first<=last, state unknown/submitted. No rebuild field or replacement tx.
- `Cursor`: `generation uint32; height int32; hash string; scan_digest string; complete_to_height int32; complete_to_hash string`. Height -1 has empty hash and initialized scan digest; complete_to_height -1/empty means no complete captured-tip scan yet. Heights never exceed MaxInt32. Generation0..16 starts at0. complete_to_height/hash retain the last fully scanned captured tip (<=height), or -1/empty initially. An event cursor that selects an Anchor seals complete_to_height/hash exactly to that anchor: its prefix is complete and scanning for that event stops there. A cursor is evidence of a locally verified contiguous prefix, not a portable absence proof. Status.scan_tip_height is the last coherent chain observation tip height, or -1 when no such tip is retained; it is not a claim of scan completion.
- `Tip`: `height uint32; hash string`.
- `Anchor`: `height uint32; hash string; header string; txid string; raw_tx_digest string; raw_tx_size uint32; tx_count uint32; tx_index uint32; output_index uint32; payload string; merkle_branch []string`. Header exactly160 hex; raw_tx_digest is single SHA256 of the full exact wire transaction including witness, raw_tx_size1..4,000,000; tx_count1..1,000,000 and tx_index<tx_count; output_index is bounded by the parsed transaction. Payload exactly146 lowercase hex encoding the expected73 bytes. Merkle siblings<=20, each display-order hash64; the path is the exact Bitcoin txid (nonwitness) tree including duplicate-right behavior derived from tx_count/index. No full foreign transaction is retained in this DTO and no first matching carrier is skipped for size. This is a **compact local observation**, not a self-contained payload-inclusion proof: full raw block/output validation establishes it, and later target/finality checks refetch that block. Raw digest/size bind the witness serialization; the Merkle branch alone only binds txid. Export/package verification must obtain the full public anchor block to independently verify payload inclusion.
- `ScanRestart`: `generation uint32; previous Cursor; observed_at_ms int64; observed_tip Tip; replacement_hash string`. Generation1..16 equals previous.generation+1. Replacement hash is the coherent current canonical hash at previous.height; empty only if current tip is below that height. Previous height must be>=0 and its hash differs from replacement, or the tip is lower. Preserve the exact old prefix/digest/completeness fields; never reinterpret them as observations of the new chain.
- `Target`: `height uint32; hash string; header string; observed_at_ms int64; observed_tip Tip`.
- `Finality`: `checkpoint chaincfg.SignedCheckpoint; observed_at_ms int64; observed_tip Tip; target_descendants uint32`. The existing checkpoint's canonical JSON order/encoding is unchanged. It must sign exactly retained targetheight/hash with the separately pinned fixture checkpoint key; descendants=tip.height-target.height>=60.
- `Conflict`: `kind string; observed_at_ms int64; declaration *SignedDeclaration; checkpoint *chaincfg.SignedCheckpoint; expected_height uint32; expected_hash string; observed_hash string; observed_tip *Tip`. Exactly one of: `declaration` has declaration non-null/other payload pointers null and height0/hash strings empty; `checkpoint` has checkpoint non-null and others absent/empty; `chain` has both auth pointers null, tip non-null, exact differing expected/observed canonical hash at a relevant height. A missing historical block below a previously observed height is unavailable until the node coherently proves its best height regressed; that coherent regression is chain conflict with observed_hash empty and tip below expected height. No unauthenticated carrier creates a declaration conflict.
- `Observation`: `observed_at_ms int64; chain_observed_at_ms int64; tip *Tip; node_state string; target_descendants uint32; current_finality bool`. Node state=`unobserved|online|offline|unavailable` describes the last explicit chain attempt. observed_at_ms is that attempt time; chain_observed_at_ms is the last coherent successful chain observation time (0 before one), and tip is null iff that latter time is0. An offline/unavailable attempt preserves the last coherent tip, descendants, eligibility and chain_observed_at_ms while advancing only attempt time/state when authorized. This is not a complete RPC transcript. Metadata operations never advance either field.
- `Record`: `version uint32=1; store_id string; event_key string; source_receipt gymevent.SnapshotReceipt; declaration SignedDeclaration; prepared_at_ms int64; publication *Publication; cursor Cursor; scan_restarts []ScanRestart; anchor *Anchor; target *Target; checkpoint *chaincfg.SignedCheckpoint; finality *Finality; conflicts []Conflict; conflict_overflow bool; incident_at_ms int64; observation Observation`.
- `Status`: `version uint32=1; store_id string; event_key string; event gymevent.Event; exists bool; phase string; publication_state string; scan_height int32; scan_tip_height int32; anchor_height uint32; anchor_hash string; target_height uint32; target_hash string; target_descendants uint32; checkpoint_present bool; finalized_at_ms int64; conflict_count uint32; conflict_overflow bool; incident_at_ms int64; prepared_at_ms int64; observed_at_ms int64; chain_observed_at_ms int64; node_state string; funding_state string; current_finality bool; escalation_due bool; scan_generation uint32; funding_generation uint32`.
- `HistoryPage`: `version uint32=1; store_id string; after_event_key string; next_event_key string; has_more bool; observed_at_ms int64; events []Status`.

Phases=`absent|prepared|waiting_anchor|waiting_target|provisional|finalized|conflict`. Conflict takes precedence; then retained Finality; then Target; then Anchor; then Publication; then prepared. `publication_state`=`none|retained|unknown|submitted`. Funding state=`unobserved|scanning|ready|waiting_for_funds|unavailable`; it is an observation, never an instruction to fund automatically. Status.observed_at_ms is the local authorized/deadline observation, while chain_observed_at_ms and node_state/descendants/current_finality come from the retained explicit chain observation. Status/History/Read/Open and UI polls do not imply a fresh chain check. HelperSnapshot live owned-node availability is separate from this record. Absent Status is derived without allocating an event; IDs/event are derived, scan heights-1, other optional hashes/times/counts empty/0, flags false **except escalation_due computed by §7**, node/funding unobserved. Snapshot/poll UI states belong to the separate helper contract.

Record.scan_restarts has0..16 entries in generation order and Cursor.generation equals its length. Funding restart history is global metadata,0..16 entries, with the same relation to funding_cursor.generation. Resetting a scan preserves all prior observations and uses the same genesis floor; it does not create a new declaration or seed. Complete local inventory may be temporarily unavailable while rebuilding.

The signed-height parser paths are Info.funding_height; Cursor.height and Cursor.complete_to_height (including every ScanRestart.previous); Status.scan_height and Status.scan_tip_height (including HistoryPage.events). Only these permit -1; no other public numeric field accepts a negative value. All timestamps are0 only for explicitly absent/initial values and otherwise1..8,640,000,000,000,000. Heights/counts additionally obey their stated int32/array bounds.

The unchanged `chaincfg.SignedCheckpoint` canonical JSON order is `version uint32=1; network uint32; genesis string64; height int32=1..MaxInt32; hash string64; signature string128` (signature is lowercase hexadecimal, not base64). Genesis/hash are nonzero display-order hex. Its existing Ed25519 message is ASCII `SLUG signed checkpoint` +NUL +LE32(version)+LE32(network)+**internal wire-order** genesis32+LE32(height)+internal wire-order hash32. Do not substitute the display-order `ID` rule used by the new declaration domains. Max encoded checkpoint4096 bytes includes transport whitespace; canonical output follows the existing encoder.

## 4. Signatures, carrier and fixed transaction

`DeclarationID=H("SLUG candidate seed declaration id\0v1\0"||LP(J(Declaration)))`. Ed25519 signs `"SLUG candidate seed declaration\0v1\0"||LP(J(Declaration))`; its signature is not part of DeclarationID. A qualifying payload is the exact73 bytes `ASCII("SLUGSEED") || byte(1) || ID(EventKey) || ID(DeclarationID)`. Require a minimally encoded OP_RETURN plus exactly that one push, no trailing opcodes. A matching payload relayed by another valid transaction has the same declaration/target identity; do not require the local transaction's txid to find the first anchor.

Normal local transaction: version2, locktime0, exactly one input using the selected confirmed funding coin, empty scriptSig, sequence0xffffffff; output0 value0 exact qualifying OP_RETURN; output1 value=`coin.value-1000` to the exact funding P2WPKH script. Reject values that cannot pay fee plus the standard nondust change. Witness is the two-item standard compressed-key P2WPKH stack: deterministic RFC6979-HMAC-SHA256 ECDSA over the BIP143 SIGHASH_ALL digest, normalized low-S DER plus byte01, then compressed public key. BIP143 scriptCode is the exact P2PKH script for HASH160 of that key; amount is the selected output value. The standard relay nondust change minimum is294 satoshis at the unchanged1000 sat/kB policy; coin value must therefore be at least1294. Normal segwit must be active for the next block; immature activation returns seed_not_mature. Only this transaction shape is signable. No arbitrary destination, amount, inputs, fee rate, RBF or key. Signatures may be validated with the existing script engine; all full raw bytes are retained after their first successful sync, regardless of retry.

Funding inventory is a bounded complete chain scan to an explicitly observed tip, described in §6. For a **new** Publication, Publish captures a coherent current tip T and requires the retained funding cursor exactly T.height/hash, funding_complete true, and the same generation. Otherwise return seed_scan_incomplete without signing/selecting. Selection is defined against that captured T, not an unstable future tip: ordinary extension after T is allowed if T and the inventory generation remain canonical through the final pre-dispatch checks; any reorg requires reconciliation/rebuild first. A new coin in a later extension does not retroactively change selection. Coinbase spend maturity uses next-block height: T.height+1-coin.block_height>=100; ordinary coins require coin.block_height<=T.height. Select the lexicographically smallest `(display txid,index)` currently unreserved mature spendable coin in that inventory. Coinbase maturity is the unchanged normal chain rule; ordinary coins require at least one confirmation. Before signing and before dispatch, query and validate that exact output still exists with the expected value/script. An unavailable or mismatched output cannot trigger silent reselection after a Publication exists. Every retained Publication reserves its input for the journal lifetime, including unknown, rejected, submitted, unconfirmed and already-confirmed outcomes; no lost ACK or spent input releases/reselects it. The global reservation table is bounded by256 event records and excluded from every new selection. A confirmed same-script change output can later fund a different event only after a complete canonical scan and maturity/unspent checks; it never replaces the original event transaction. Funds outside the fixed script are never inspected or spent.

Pure parsing distinguishes structural signed statements from supported declarations. A different digest/rule/store in a correctly signed version1 statement for the same fixed EventKey is authenticated equivocation, not a silently unsupported statement to ignore. Main Record validation additionally requires its declaration to equal the exact builder result from this Pin and concrete source receipt. Unknown versions cannot acquire authority. The system has no global declaration feed; it detects signed equivocation it actually receives, not proof of worldwide uniqueness. Unknown third-party payload digests are ignored as unauthenticated; an exact known signed declaration payload is qualifying.

## 5. Exact API surface

Core uses concrete sources; no receipt import or caller-provided block verdict exists. Constructor clocks are private time.Now; scoped tagged wrappers may follow the existing Set44 testclock pattern only for test composition.

```
Create(ctx context.Context, path string, pin Pin, events *gymevent.Store) (*Store,error)
Open(ctx context.Context, path string, expected Pin, events *gymevent.Store) (*Store,error)
ResumePrepared(ctx context.Context, path string, expected Pin, events *gymevent.Store) (*Store,error)
(*Store).Close() error
(*Store).Info(ctx context.Context) (Info,error)
(*Store).Prepare(ctx context.Context, events *gymevent.Store, entries *gymentry.Store, session gymstable.Session, saturday string) (Record,error)
(*Store).Publish(ctx context.Context, events *gymevent.Store, entries *gymentry.Store, session gymstable.Session, publisher *seednode.Publisher, saturday string) (Record,error)
(*Store).Reconcile(ctx context.Context, events *gymevent.Store, entries *gymentry.Store, session gymstable.Session, publisher *seednode.Publisher, saturday string) (Record,error)
(*Store).Attest(ctx context.Context, events *gymevent.Store, entries *gymentry.Store, session gymstable.Session, publisher *seednode.Publisher, saturday string) (Record,error)
(*Store).Status(ctx context.Context, events *gymevent.Store, entries *gymentry.Store, session gymstable.Session, saturday string) (Status,error)
(*Store).Record(ctx context.Context, events *gymevent.Store, entries *gymentry.Store, session gymstable.Session, saturday string) (Record,error)
(*Store).History(ctx context.Context, events *gymevent.Store, entries *gymentry.Store, session gymstable.Session, afterEventKey string, limit uint32) (HistoryPage,error)
(*Store).ObserveCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, events *gymevent.Store, entries *gymentry.Store, session gymstable.Session, saturday string, checkpoint chaincfg.SignedCheckpoint) (Record,error)
(*Store).ObserveEquivocation(ctx context.Context, events *gymevent.Store, entries *gymentry.Store, session gymstable.Session, saturday string, statement SignedDeclaration) (Record,error)
```

ObserveCheckpoint/ObserveEquivocation accept only bounded public signed evidence for an already prepared event; they do not create events. They are core/service-test evidence APIs, not generic browser import commands. ObserveCheckpoint stores a matching certificate but cannot create Finality without node verification; Attest performs that verification and purpose-limited fixture signing. Reconcile verifies an already retained certificate but never signs, sends a transaction or fetches a key.

Pure API signatures are exact:

```go
func CandidatePin(source gymevent.Pin) (Pin, error)
func ID(Pin) (string, error)
func EventKey(Pin, gymevent.Event) (string, error)
func RulesID() string
func DeclarationID(Declaration) (string, error)
func RecordDigest(Pin, Record) (string, error)
func ValidatePin(Pin) (Pin, error)
func MarshalPin(Pin) ([]byte, error)
func ParsePin([]byte) (Pin, error)
```

For every named DTO X in §3 except Pin, expose exactly `ValidateX(expected Pin, value X) (X,error)`, `MarshalX(expected Pin,value X) ([]byte,error)`, `ParseX(expected Pin,raw []byte) (X,error)`. Shared seednode aliases have the same gymseed codec names. Validate returns a bounded owned value; Marshal returns canonical bytes without LF. Parse accepts bounded field-order/whitespace transport but every declared decoded key exactly once. Standalone child validators check local shape and all available expected-Pin facts; cross-object facts needing a Record (expected payload, target relation, timestamp correlation, restart chain, phase) are enforced by ValidateRecord, not invented from absent context. Structural SignedDeclaration validation verifies the pinned publisher and exact source-event conflict key while permitting a well-formed alternate rule/snapshot/store declaration as authenticated conflict evidence. Main Record validation requires exact compiled CandidatePin/builder declaration/source receipt equality. RulesID and CandidatePin never accept caller fixture/rule overrides.

`DeclarationID` validates its context-independent closed structural form before hashing. `RecordDigest=H("SLUG candidate seed record\0v1\0"||LP(J(Record)))`; it changes with observations and is not a replacement seed identity. Completed helper jobs retain their exact returned Record bytes.

## 6. Bounded chain and funding scan

The concrete node adapter has only bounded identity/tip/canonical hash/raw block/header/unspent-output/peer inspection, exact fixed-transaction submission, and purpose-fixed fixture signature operations. It is attached by the actual owned zero256 process manager; no public generic endpoint factory feeds the core. Verify normal profile, network/genesis, exact pinned child marker/home, live owned primary/peer processes, literal loopback RPC and exclusive owned loopback peer topology. Config credentials never enter errors, journal, DTOs or logs. A node response alone is not ownership evidence. The concrete attachment constructor and cancellation/join lifetime are specified in §6.1 and the helper contract; both must pass joint review before approval.

Each Reconcile captures one identity-checked tip. It processes at most eight distinct full blocks serially in that call, starting at the smallest next needed height of the funding cursor and this event cursor. Read raw full blocks with numeric verbosity0; strictly bound hex/decoded byte count before allocation, parse exact wire consumption, verify header Argon2id using normal256MiB profile, hash/height/canonical identity, parent continuity and all transaction IDs/Merkle root. Do not substitute a txindex search or header-only result. The trusted full node remains responsible for consensus validity/difficulty progression; this adapter is not a second consensus engine.

Advance each cursor only over its next contiguous block; when both need that height, process it once for both. All outputs are inspected in tx index then output index order. Funding scanning adds matching script outputs and removes spent outpoints; max128 unspent tracked coins, checked before mutation. Coinbase flags and mined heights come from complete blocks, not caller summaries. Empty inventory is meaningful only after a complete captured-tip scan. The event scan finds the first exact qualifying payload; within a block use smallest `(tx_index,output_index)`. Scan index/count/reference validation precedes allocation. No anchor is selected while any earlier height remains missing or uncertain.

Per-block event scan fold starts `H("SLUG candidate seed scan\0v1\0"||ID(StoreID)||ID(EventKey)||LE32(generation)||LE32(0)||ID(Genesis))`; append each processed block as `H("SLUG candidate seed scan step\0v1\0"||priorRaw32||LE32(height)||ID(hash))`. Funding starts `H("SLUG candidate funding scan\0v1\0"||ID(StoreID)||LE32(generation)||LE32(0)||ID(Genesis))` and uses the same step construction/domain `SLUG candidate funding scan step\0v1\0`. These are local journal continuity checks, not portable non-inclusion proofs.

Before committing a batch, recheck chain identity, original cursor hashes, every processed height/hash (max8), original captured tip membership and final anchor/target references. Reserve any required anchor/target revalidation from the same eight-block budget before scanning new heights. For an event that finds its first anchor at A under captured tipH>A, commit cursor.height=A and complete_to_height=A (hashes both anchor): this is complete prefix0..A only, never an H-completeness claim. Funding complete is separately true only when its own cursor reached its captured tip. Normal tip extension is allowed; mixed-branch responses refuse. Never hold account/source/seed mutexes over RPC/hash work. Persist cursor/inventory/anchor transitions only after the final original-session source lease. A node change after this observation remains possible; the next operation rechecks.

A coherent canonical mismatch at the **pinned anchor or target height/hash** latches permanent event conflict; neither is replaced. A reorg strictly above an unchanged anchor/target is not seed replacement: refresh current descendant count/current eligibility, retain first historical Finality. Missing RPC data alone is unavailable, not automatically conflict. A coherent shorter chain below a pinned anchor/target is relevant chain conflict, with its exact observed tip retained.

An unanchored event cursor on an orphaned branch may restart at the same genesis floor: append one ScanRestart, increment generation, reset height/complete_to_height=-1 and hashes empty, initialize a new generation-labelled scan digest, and later scan normal bounded steps. No declaration/Publication changes. Once Anchor exists the event cursor stops exactly at its height; there is no post-target event scan cursor. A global funding-cursor reorg independently appends a funding ScanRestart, clears only the unspent inventory, increments generation and restarts at genesis; **all Publication bytes and reservations survive**. It does not mark unrelated events conflicted. Each of the two histories allows16 restarts; exhaustion refuses further scan advancement with seed_capacity and leaves all earlier evidence, never false completeness or a synthetic seed conflict. No truncation/overwrite/reset command exists. Detect and record a required restart as a bounded mutation with zero new block bodies; the next Reconcile resumes scanning. Chain instability discovered during an uncommitted batch discards that batch without cursor advancement; only a coherent mismatch against a retained cursor may create a restart.

A retained publication input later orphaned/spent does not authorize replacement. Reconcile may still discover its unchanged carrier, otherwise reports retained publication/unavailable funding. This alone is not authenticated event conflict. Unlimited bounded steps are permitted; reaching a work/time/capacity bound never means the scan completed.

### 6.1 Concrete process attachment and bounded RPC

`seednode` imports existing source types but **never gymseed**, avoiding a package cycle. Pure `seednode.ChainIdentityFor(source gymevent.Pin)` validates the fixed two-fixture source and derives zero256 identity, normal network/genesis and PublisherChainID exactly as §2; CandidatePin calls this one implementation. `gymseed` checks the Publisher's immutable identity equals CandidatePin before every operation. This is a trusted in-process owner API, not cryptographic attestation against malicious Go code or a compromised operating system.

```go
// Non-wire ownership inputs, never JSON/config/browser fields.
type OwnedProcess struct { Cmd *exec.Cmd; Done <-chan struct{} }
type OwnerBinding struct {
    Source gymevent.Pin
    Home string // canonical absolute validated zero256 child directory
    Primary OwnedProcess
    Peer OwnedProcess
}
type ChainIdentity struct {
    SourceStoreID, PublisherAccountID, PublisherSourceAuthorityID string
    PublisherChainID string
    Network uint32
    Genesis string
}
func ChainIdentityFor(gymevent.Pin) (ChainIdentity, error)
func AttachOwned(ctx context.Context, binding OwnerBinding) (*Publisher, error)
func (p *Publisher) Identity() ChainIdentity
func (p *Publisher) Close() error
```

Only the existing pilot process owner calls AttachOwned, using its retained actual `childNode.cmd` and `done` channels after ready startup and holding the scoped lifecycle borrow. Do not read Cmd.ProcessState concurrently with the Wait goroutine; observe Done for exit. Validate nonnil live Process/PID, distinct primary/peer, unchanged command executable/config argument, safe real Home and exact primary.conf/peer.conf under it, each config<=8KiB, same-file opened regular-file checks and closed expected options matching the existing startNode-generated configuration. Derive RPC user/password/ports and chain datadirs from those exact owned configurations; never accept an RPCURL/credentials/verifiedBool callback in the public constructor. Copy only bounded parsed private connection values; do not export/log credentials. Validate normal network/genesis/activation rules on both, primary datadir `<Home>/primary-chain`, peer `<Home>/peer-chain`, exact startNode topology: primary has nolisten=1 and one connect to the peer owned listener; peer has its owned loopback listen plus one connect to the fourth generated unused loopback port (not a primary listener). The four generated ports are distinct; no external/DNS/additional connect/listen is allowed. The sole actual primary peer is outbound to that owned peer listener; the peer has one inbound loopback connection from primary. The intentionally unused peer connect is permitted, never treated as an external fallback. Validate this actual paired relation and reject any additional peer. The trusted owner establishes process/config provenance; RPC checks establish current consistency, not hostile-host security. If node startup has not reached the exact peer relation yet, return offline/unavailable rather than weaken topology.

Attach creates its own cancellable child context of the caller borrow, owns only bounded RPC clients, and does not own or stop the actual nodes. Any Done closes/cancels attachment. Publisher.Close cancels and joins its actual outstanding RPC/hash work before returning; owner then performs unchanged node Close. No caller retains attachment across an operation, switch or restart. Root's new route uses a private `pilotNodes` borrow method; old process startup/stop/default routes remain unchanged.

The adapter's public operations are purpose-limited: `Observe(ctx) (Tip,error)`, `CanonicalHash(ctx,height uint32) (string,error)`, `Block(ctx,height uint32) (*wire.MsgBlock,error)` returning an owned fully checked block, `Unspent(ctx,outpoint Outpoint) (*UnspentOutput,error)`, `BuildPublication(ctx,carrier [73]byte,coin FundingCoin) ([]byte,error)`, `SubmitPublication(ctx,carrier [73]byte,coin FundingCoin,raw []byte) (string,error)`, and `AttestTarget(ctx,anchor Anchor,target HeaderRef) (chaincfg.SignedCheckpoint,Tip,error)`. `HeaderRef` fields are Height uint32/Hash string/Header string. Tip/Outpoint/FundingCoin/Anchor are the exact §3 shapes owned in seednode and re-exported by gymseed aliases; UnspentOutput fields are ValueSatoshis int64/Script string/Confirmations uint32/Coinbase bool/BestBlock string. These are concrete methods, not caller-injected interfaces. Core exclusively supplies the known carrier, journal-selected coin and retained anchor/target; adapter still validates fixed funding script/amount/carrier syntax/transaction shape and actual node facts. AttestTarget re-fetches the anchor, verifies the exact supplied known carrier, target parent and current canonical depth>=60; it signs only that target. No general message, checkpoint, destination, raw RPC or arbitrary transaction signer exists.

RPC allowlist is getcurrentnet, getblockchaininfo, getblockhash, getbestblock, getblockheader, getblock (numeric verbosity0), gettxout (include_mempool=true), getpeerinfo, and **only SubmitPublication** sendrawtransaction. No generation, submitblock, wallet, listunspent, searchrawtransactions, addnode, invalidateblock or checkpoint-install RPC exists in this adapter. `gettxout` values accept bounded ordinary JSON numeric notation including exponent form emitted by the existing RPC float encoder (for example1e-8); normalize using exact decimal integer arithmetic to satoshis, rejecting a fractional satoshi, negative/overflow amount, excess numeric-token length128 or exponent magnitude>32. Never convert via binary floating point; validate script/value/coinbase and returned bestblock against a coherent observed chain. A null mempool-aware output cannot authorize signing/dispatch or a new input. Raw tx reply acknowledgment is lowercase exact retained txid; malformed/HTTP/JSON/RPC error after possible dispatch is unknown. There is no automatic transport retry.

All body responses have method-specific bounds: small identity/hash/UTXO replies<=64KiB, peer list<=8 entries/64KiB, raw block hex<=8,000,000 characters plus8KiB JSON overhead, header160 hex. Check Content-Length when present and bounded streaming read regardless. TLS is inapplicable to the fixed literal-loopback HTTP owner connection; no configurable endpoint/proxy/redirect. Bracket mutable operations with exact owned identity/topology and canonical references; the final check still cannot stop a future reorg, which is why subsequent observations remain explicit.

The eight-block/normal-Argon budget includes anchor refetch and target-header checks as well as new scan blocks. Reuse identical already checked block/header within the operation; if the budget is exhausted, persist only a coherent prefix and defer discovering target/finality to another explicit bounded Reconcile. Do not claim a target absent merely because this step reached its resource budget. No more than one full block/256MiB Argon workspace is live at a time; any returned block is released before fetching the next.

## 7. Target and finality

Pin anchor and its completeness cursor atomically. Checked `targetHeight=anchorHeight+1` must fit positive int32. Target is accepted only when the exact canonical block at that height has the pinned anchor hash as parent, normal verified header hash and a bracketed current membership observation. Pin its first hash/header forever. A late observer may discover anchor and target together; this is legitimate recovery, not proof of universal prior ignorance.

Before accepting a Target or checking Finality, refetch and fully verify the retained Anchor block and exact transaction/output, raw digest/size, tx count, payload and Merkle path. Never infer payload inclusion from the compact observation alone. Reconcile may update descendant observations and, when a previously stored matching checkpoint exists, create Finality only after identity/ancestry/membership checks prove target is currently canonical with `tip.height-target.height>=60`. Checkpoint.Verify uses normal network/genesis plus the **separately pinned candidate fixture public key**. A checkpoint for another height is inapplicable; a valid competing hash at the exact target height is authenticated conflict. Existing node `getcheckpointinfo` status and the old height1 record are never accepted as substitutes. No checkpoint is loaded into the node, and no consensus input changes.

Attest is an explicit zero256 fresh/unheld SeedPublish action plus the correct owned publisher. It derives the retained target (never accepts header/height/JSON), verifies canonical anchor→target and>=60 descendants, then signs only that exact normal-format checkpoint with the fixed candidate fixture key outside the account lease. Final original-session guard persists the certificate and Finality atomically after a last bounded chain recheck. A failure before any durable mutation is definite; uncertain commit or revocation after a successful callback is outcome_unknown. Replaying an existing certificate never changes its signature/evidence. Reconcile remains held-compatible and never produces a signature.

Retained Finality is historical evidence, not a permanent node-consensus assertion. Later chain/authenticated-declaration/checkpoint conflict takes precedence and is never erased by a subsequent matching response. Temporary node outage alone does not erase first finality evidence. Store latest node availability and `current_finality` separately. It records eligibility **at chain_observed_at_ms**, not timeless present truth: true only for that coherent chain observation with matching certificate, unchanged anchor/target, >=60 descendants and no conflict. A later coherent above-target reorg/depth<60 makes it false; an offline/unavailable attempt preserves the last observed value/time and explicitly marks availability. A newly latched authenticated conflict makes eligibility false regardless of prior chain observation. Neither operation deletes historical Finality or changes its bytes; relevant conflict overrides phase. A new Finality is never fabricated offline.

At/after the event's exact following-calendar-Saturday noon, if there is no retained Finality or conflict is latched, set the first immutable incident_at_ms from the trusted monotonic local clock. This is candidate escalation for unresolved required seed evidence, not cancellation or replacement. Once set it persists even after later valid evidence. New Status/Record/History/Prepare/Publish/Reconcile/Attest observations perform this bounded local deadline update; polls use helper cache only. `Status.escalation_due` is `(observed_at_ms>=event.incident_deadline_ms) && (no historical Finality || relevant conflict)`, using the existing Event.IncidentDeadlineMS / incident_deadline_ms field. A missing seed Record derives escalation_due from the trusted current observation but incident_at_ms remains0 because no first incident has been journaled; exists=false never implies a complete source/seed. Prepared records atomically latch their actual first incident_at_ms, which persists. Local outage, stale latest observation, or depth temporarily below60 **after historical Finality alone does not trigger escalation**; D77 says not finalized by the next Saturday, and the historical record stands absent relevant conflict. UI distinguishes “escalation due; no publication record” from a journaled first incident and separately shows current availability/depth.

## 8. Linearization, authorization and unknown outcomes

Lock order is seed resource gate → event gate → entry (and, when existing code needs it, stable) gates → original account lease → entry/event mutexes → seed mutex. Never acquire a source gate while holding an outer account lease. Store methods borrow sources/publisher per call and retain no caller session or child handle.

Add only these concrete source seams (new files; old methods unchanged). `gymevent.SeedSourceInfo` is an owned internal Go value, not a wire DTO: `Version uint32; StoreID string; Pin gymevent.Pin; ObservedAtMS int64; ParticipantAccountID string; ParticipantGymID string`. Its StoreID/Pin are the concrete event store, participant IDs derive from the exact matched entry Pin, and ObservedAtMS is the final synchronized event/entry observation.

```go
// gymentry: cap is only gymaccount.View or gymaccount.SeedPublish.
func (s *Store) WithSeedView(ctx context.Context, session gymstable.Session,
    cap gymaccount.Capability,
    fn func(SnapshotSourceInfo, func() error) error) error
// gymevent: same restricted cap, same original participant and concrete source.
func (s *Store) WithSeedView(ctx context.Context, source *gymentry.Store,
    session gymstable.Session, cap gymaccount.Capability,
    fn func(SeedSourceInfo, func() error) error) error
func (s *Store) WithSeedSnapshot(ctx context.Context, source *gymentry.Store,
    session gymstable.Session, saturday string,
    prepare func(SnapshotReceipt) (func(SeedSourceInfo, func() error) error, error)) error
```

Entry WithSeedView mirrors WithSnapshotView but validates the restricted cap and, for SeedPublish, requires the exact published zero256 identity. It acquires the entry resource gate, original capability lease, entry mutex and clock observation in that order; its callback receives the existing final check. Event WithSeedView acquires its own gate first, calls the concrete entry seam, validates full participant Pin, observes event clock and then invokes the foreign callback. It never performs source/sign/hash work after that callback. Account SeedPublish is added to validCapability **and heldCapability**, so existing authentication freshness/hold checks apply; accountpilot.withCapability also applies its signed_in/nonbusy guard to SeedPublish. Mining-token and un-enrolled/recovery-required refusals remain unchanged.

WithSeedSnapshot holds the event gate, does an initial original View check, loads and semantically validates its own complete immutable receipt outside the account lease, and invokes prepare with an owned copy. Prepare performs any canonical/crypto work and returns a final synchronous callback. The final original View lease then verifies the exact receipt remains the same, observes source clocks, and invokes that callback. Comparing precomputed canonical receipt bytes/digest is permitted; rerunning condition/manifest projection or signature work under the lease is not. Final metadata comparison may use already loaded immutable receipt state; no arbitrary JSON or supplied receipt establishes provenance. On any prepare error no foreign callback executes.

All seams propagate callback errors even if a trusted wrapper returns nil, check cancellation/original View before disclosure, and never reenter source/account/store from callbacks. Seed caller tracks whether its foreign write succeeded and maps any subsequent outer/context failure to outcome_unknown. Expensive public semantic validation runs before the final callback. There is no extra source write after a foreign commit.

Prepare authenticates first, refuses incomplete/too-late source or seed activation, and preflights full record/reservation/signature outside the lease. Idempotent replay returns the exact original declaration/receipt after authorization and final original-view check; it does not resign or replace the source. The final callback observes/persists local clock at least the source observation, stores first prepared record and event count atomically, and observes deadline. It does not sign or draw inside the lease.

Publish first verifies fresh/unheld zero256 and matching publisher ownership. A latched relevant conflict refuses with seed_conflict. If an Anchor is already retained, return the authorized retained Record without signing, reserving, arming or retransmitting: publication is already anchored. A retained transaction whose input is no longer unspent remains reserved and is never rebuilt/reselected; read-only Reconcile may discover its eventual inclusion. If no Publication exists, it validates complete funding inventory, fixed chosen coin and exact transaction shape, signs outside leases, then syncs the immutable raw transaction and reservation under a final original SeedPublish guard. Before every actual send, a separate final guarded atomic write increments bounded dispatch_count and sets unknown. This **durable exact-transaction dispatch intent** is the authorization linearization point. Release all account/store mutexes, check task context immediately before transport, then dispatch the same bytes. Reset/cancellation after the intent may coincide with an already sent transaction; return unknown and retain it. No promise of atomic network revocation is made. No new send is permitted under a held/expired/replaced session.

After any possible network dispatch, transport error, malformed reply, changed identity, cancellation or failed final authorization is outcome_unknown. Successful txid acknowledgment may be stored as submitted only after matching the exact retained txid and final same-session guard; it is not inclusion. Already-in-mempool/chain errors do not select new bytes. Query/scan first or repeat the identical transaction only through a newly authorized Publish. Reconcile never transmits. If the retained funding output is gone and the carrier not yet found, preserve the transaction and report conflict/unavailable according to verified evidence; never choose another input.

All source/seed clocks reject rollback and preserve highwater on known rejections when allowed by the original authorization. Within **each** source-lease invocation, every source observation precedes its foreign callback and no source mutation follows that callback before return. Publish deliberately has distinct raw-tx, dispatch-intent and ACK invocations; a later specified transition may reacquire the same original session and observe its source before its own callback. Any failure after an earlier durable transition preserves that transition and reports the specified uncertainty; it does not roll back or reselect. Write errors poison until explicit reopen; Close cancels and joins real owned work. Final native disclosure always rechecks the same original View. Public signed-evidence acceptance never makes a different account/source Pin trusted.

## 9. Storage, bounds and audit

Schema1 marker `SLUG-CANDIDATE-SEEDS.json`, exact ordered fields `application:"slug-candidate-seeds", version:1, store_id, pin`, canonical JSON plus LF, <=20KiB. Directory contains only marker and LevelDB `db`; reject symlink ancestors/entries and wrong/missing established state. Initialization exact sequence: validate normal profile/Pin and concrete event Info match before effects; require an absent path or real empty directory; atomically create/fsync exact marker plus directory; create owned LevelDB; sync sole `init` key with canonical ordered `version uint32=1; store_id string; pin Pin`; only **after that durable intent** sample/validate actual now; sync one batch deleting init and writing initial meta (created_at_ms=clock_ms=now, event_count0, generation0 cursor at-1, empty restarts/inventory/reservations, last_funding_tip null). Sync owned directory boundaries. No earlier sampled time may be carried across intent fsync. Return only after final write success; any uncertain write preserves files and returns unknown/poisoned.

Ordinary Open requires exact marker and initialized canonical meta/audit, never completes initialization. ResumePrepared is only the parent's already-held prepared latch path with independently reconstructed expected Pin: absent/real empty path runs Create; exact matching marker-only directory or matching marker+empty DB may continue the above intent creation; exact matching init-only DB continues with a fresh actual time; fully initialized-empty DB opens preserving original time. The only filesystem entries allowed are exact marker and actual LevelDB-owned db directory; unknown/symlink/partial application keys refuse. An initialized state is adoptable as prepared-empty only if event_count0, initial unobserved funding cursor, no history/inventory/reservations and no extra keys. Event-bearing state is never adopted as empty, and ready-missing never recreates. Do not delete arbitrary partial files or alter44 source state.

DB keys: `init`, `meta`, `r||raw32(EventKey)`, `f||raw32(txid)||BE32(index)` for unspent funding inventory, `u||raw32(txid)||BE32(index)` for a retained publication reservation→raw32(EventKey). No unknown/nested keys. Metadata exact canonical order/types: `version uint32=1; store_id string; pin Pin; created_at_ms int64; clock_ms int64; event_count uint32; funding_cursor Cursor; funding_restarts []ScanRestart; funding_complete bool; last_funding_tip *Tip`. last_funding_tip is null initially, otherwise the last coherently captured funding scan target, which may exceed a partial cursor; funding_complete iff cursor reached that captured tip in the same generation. Meta.clock_ms>=created_at_ms and every retained local timestamp. Info is a pure owned metadata copy and performs no source/node/clock advancement. FundingCoin values and every Record are canonical JSON; reservation values are exactly raw32(EventKey). Max metadata40KiB (full Pin plus16 restart observations); initialized meta excludes init. Each full Record <=224KiB; max256 records; funding<=128 rows each512B; reservations<=256 keys. Fixed remaining future record growth is reserved at Prepare, independent of current serialized length. Total logical values plus keys and marker are below64MiB; LevelDB physical overhead is not represented as logical bytes.

Max Pin16KiB, ScanRestart1024B,16 restarts per scan, Declaration4KiB, SignedDeclaration5KiB, local raw transaction1024 bytes, checkpoint4096B, Conflict8KiB, conflicts8, History8 statuses, Status8KiB, API response<256KiB including envelope/LF. Parser depth<=16, field names<=64, closed exact fields and command-correlated nulls. Raw hex bounds precede decode; block RPC result ceiling allows only wire4,000,000 bytes plus JSON framing, never an arbitrary16MiB body. Max operation30s, RPC10s, one in-flight request, one block working set/one serial Argon at a time; no redirect/proxy/retry/insecure TLS. Literal loopback HTTP is restricted to the owned process capability; no public RPC config surface.

Deduplicate conflicts by kind plus canonical signed statement/checkpoint or the exact chain height/expected/observed/tip tuple, excluding observed_at_ms. Retain the first observation time and append at most8 distinct conflicts; a ninth distinct valid conflict sets conflict_overflow=true without dropping any earlier payload. Overflow is valid only with8 retained conflicts and is permanently conflict. A valid duplicate never resets time. ObserveCheckpoint before a target returns seed_target_unavailable; wrong-height certificate is invalid_request; wrong signature/network/key is invalid_request. A matching certificate may be retained without current maturity; only the exact node-verified action creates Finality. ObserveEquivocation requires an existing record, same EventKey and a genuinely different valid signed Declaration; exact identical declaration is an authorized no-op. No authenticated-evidence input can create an absent event.

Audit all raw counts/key/value lengths before decode, then canonical bytes, fixed Pin/IDs/rules, exact record source/declaration/signature binding, timestamps/highwaters, publication shape/reservation uniqueness, complete cursor crosslinks, anchor/target height-parent/Merkle relationship, applicable checkpoint/signature/descendant equation, conflict union/dedup/order, phase derivation and deadline invariants. Open performs no RPC, proof/Argon, signing or SVG. Source receipt semantics use existing pure Set44 checks outside publication leases. No storage audit can prove worldwide statement completeness or actual wall-clock noon.

Canonical history sorts by `(event.cutoff_ms,event_key)` ascending; limit1..8, unknown nonempty cursor errors; terminal next_event_key is empty. Only Prepare allocates records. Full record reads absent→seed_not_found; Status absent derives fields without allocation. All nil source/publisher, unknown enum/version or malformed arguments fail before effects.

## 10. Errors and helper integration

Exact exposed errors: `invalid_request`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `stale_view`, `busy`, `outcome_unknown`, `seed_unavailable`, `seed_corrupt`, `seed_capacity`, `seed_clock`, `seed_calendar`, `seed_created_too_late`, `seed_source_incomplete`, `seed_not_found`, `seed_not_prepared`, `seed_node_offline`, `seed_waiting_for_funds`, `seed_scan_incomplete`, `seed_conflict`, `seed_target_unavailable`, `seed_not_mature`, `seed_cancelled`. Closed/poisoned/profile remain internal typed errors mapped to seed_unavailable/corrupt as exact helper policy specifies; no secret/raw node error text.

Separate Seed v1 helper frames; unchanged old frame shapes and entry/event/preview APIs. Async kinds prepare/publish/reconcile/attest share the existing single active/single queued lane. One Seed job active-or-queued, one retained immutable terminal Seed result; reserve256KiB for the complete Seed family within the existing1MiB reciprocal cache budget before ACK. Existing render/export/job paths must account for the reservation. Polls/metadata cannot call network or hash work. No generic browser raw transaction/checkpoint/declaration/funding/key input. Original view/store/event/job correlation and typed unknown outcomes survive native boundaries. Helper/native exact DTOs, v5 root installation and process-owner attachment are separate appendices requiring independent review before this core freezes.

## 11. Acceptance and provenance

Independent reference derivation follows exact freeze, using frozen Set44 public records, pinned calendar and declaration/checkpoint/funding fixture definitions. Cover canonical hashes/byte order/signatures/carrier, every parser refusal with positive control, candidate-versus-production authority mismatch, exact target maturity at59/60/61 descendants, unsupported/irrelevant/conflicting checkpoint, old height1 refusal, all phase/incident transitions and finite capacities.

Actual isolated normal-PoW tests explicitly fund key1 (other mined rewards may use an unrelated sink to respect inventory cap), produce a complete authentic44 snapshot under clearly labelled scoped clocks, seal and broadcast the exact transaction, inspect real block inclusion/first occurrence and later target, mine60 descendants, explicitly Attest and verify its signature independently. Exercise a second gym/held session/read-only reconciliation, Stop/logout/restart/offline node, wrong child chain, no funds, incomplete scan, original-token expiry/reset during build/dispatch, lost node reply, late/duplicate relays, missing and full4MiB-block earlier carriers, pre-anchor/funding-only/above-target/below-target reorg distinctions,16/17 restart cap, finality conflict, and following-Saturday/DST escalation without substitution. Tests must prove no funding/spend/mining RPC occurs through Reconcile or cache polls.

SIGKILL/uncertain-write boundaries include marker/init, sealed declaration, signed transaction/reservation, armed dispatch before network, broadcast before ACK persistence, cursor batch, anchor, target, checkpoint/finality and incident. After reopen preserve bytes/IDs/floor, keep poison/unknown semantics and never silently rebuild/reselect. Preserve failed diagnostics. No public mining, real keys, production signing, GUI/D74 or perfect-randomness claim.
